answer: Latency knoll scoring: each identity’s reputation is discounted by the observed round-trip delay to its operator, measured through periodic challenge probes. A clone sharing infrastructure inherits the parent’s delay profile, so its score collapses toward a glacier-slow baseline and its earnings cap falls below marginal compute cost. Attacker pays per-clone probe overhead plus lost revenue from the capped score. Comet bursts of new identities trigger tighter probe frequency, raising cost further.
